context: The party has just encountered Jergal in the old crypt—he climbed from his sarcophagus after the group defeated undead scholars and spoke with the player, then began to wander the burial chambers waiting for them to leave. Jergal is the emotionless, formal god of the dead, bound by Helm’s judgment to aid the party as penance for past crimes; he is effectively immortal and difficult to rile. His immediate aim is practical: he wants to see the party’s faces and intends to teleport to their camp later to offer further assistance (resurrection services and debriefing). Withers’ comments about the changed chambers, parchment and bone dust simply set the scene of an ancient, altered crypt rather than introducing new plot elements.
